Be able to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Have technical and laboratory competencies.

Be able to combine theory and practice to solve problems of strength of materials and structural calculation.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: BEHAVIOR OF REAL SOLIDS. EQUILIBRIUM AND CALCULATION OF REACTIONS IN STRUCTURES
Topic 1: SYSTEMS OF FORCES AND EQUILIBRIUM
System of forces and equivalent systems of forces
Calculation of reactions for externally isostatic structures
Calculation of reactions for externally hyperstatic structures
BLOCK II: STRESS LAWS IN ISOSTATIC STRUCTURES
Relationship between load, shear force, and bending moment
Determination of stress diagrams in straight-line elements.
Determination of stress diagrams in curved-line elements.
Determination of stress diagrams in structures with a change of directrix.
Determination of stress diagrams in isostatic frames.
BLOCK III: CONCEPT OF STRESS AND DEFORMATION. RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN STRESSES AND DEFORMATIONS IN ELASTIC SOLIDS
BLOCK IV: PRINCIPLES OF STRENGTH OF MATERIALS. GENERAL STUDY OF RESISTANT ELEMENTS
Determination of normal stresses due to axial force
Determination of normal stresses due to pure and simple bending
Determination of normal stresses due to compound bending
BLOCK V: ARTICULATED STRUCTURES AND CABLES
Cables subjected to point and distributed loads
BLOCK VI: INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL METHODS IN STRUCTURES. APPLICATIONS IN ENGINEERING
Four assessable practical sessions in the course
assessment_rules: To consider the continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 4.5 is required in the final exam, for both ordinary and extraordinary calls. To pass the course, attendance and completion of the laboratory practices scheduled in the weekly plan are mandatory. The weighting of the practical grade in the continuous assessment corresponds to what is established in the course, in accordance with the university regulations. In the Mechanics of Structures course, the weighting of the laboratory practices takes the value of 37.5% of the continuous assessment grade. In this course, students must not use artificial intelligence tools for the completion of tasks or exercises proposed by the lecturer. Academic fraud through the use of AI will be subject to the University's regulations on academic misconduct.
